Its marker survives; the filter preserves the destination while refusing three DXF versions and DWG, then successfully saves a complete material on the same filter.

System-codec focused lane: 2,070 assertions in 32 cases passed with the new isolated dylib. DYLD_PRINT_LIBRARIES verified its exact path. Existing consumer objects were compiled against the prior headers; comparison shows the installed public headers differ only in a documentation comment. The updated test translation unit was compiled and linked against the current installation.
Bundled-codec DXF round-trip lane: 4,751 assertions in 143 cases passed on the preceding consumer commit; the later test-only change is compiled only in the system-codec lane.
A separate local probe imported the three locally generated ezdxf default materials into consumer metadata and observed all three markers; an ordinary material remained unmarked.

The first test used a policy on a subclass of RS_FilterDXFRW and passed only because the old library failed to enforce the opt-in. With the fix it correctly failed: private DRW_Interface inheritance prevents the cross-cast. The corrected test uses a public codec adapter; its earlier result is superseded.

limits: The consumer intentionally refuses all exports containing a marked raw-only material until complete graph validation and same-version replay are implemented.

RS_FilterDXFRW privately inherits DRW_Interface, so production policy opt-in requires an explicitly accessible adapter or another reviewed interface design; inheriting the policy on a subclass alone does not work.
Native GUI, a full clean consumer rebuild, external semantic evidence, complete graph behavior after edits and final platform qualification remain open.
